notes:
### Missions stop honestly

- **Stop means stopped.** Pressing Stop on a mission now shows "Stopping" until every turn it was running has really ended, instead of calling it stopped at once. Nothing new starts meanwhile, and a turn that finishes after the stop can no longer finish, pass or restart the mission; what it did is kept on record so you can check it. The same goes for a mission whose hours run out mid-turn.
- **A restart during a stop never resumes work.** If the desktop restarts while a mission is stopping, Mimir finishes the stop by itself only when its record shows every turn had ended. Otherwise it asks you, saying for each cut-off turn whether its process is still running, gone, or unknown, and the mission stays stopping until you confirm. Something a turn started outside its own process, like a render, may still be running, and Mimir says so.
- **A failed turn asks before it tries again.** A turn that failed after it started may already have changed files, so the mission now asks you to look before another attempt, instead of retrying on its own.
- **Reviews must add up.** A reviewer's "pass" counts only when every check has exactly one passing entry with evidence; a pass that contradicts its own checks goes back for fixing.
- **No two writers on one file.** Assignments that own the same file under different spellings (capital letters, backslashes, `./`, a trailing dot) now take turns instead of writing at once.

### Screen control

- **Agents can see and use your screen, on every engine.** A new switch in Settings → Agent → Screen control (off by default, and off again whenever Mimir closes) gives every agent tools to look at your monitors, read their text, click, type, press keys and scroll. Claude and Codex see pictures; DeepSeek, Mimir credits and the other text models read the screen's words with their positions, and click by those.
- **You stay in charge.** Turning it on asks in Mimir's own dialog, and each look and each action still asks unless screen sight and desktop control are on in Settings → Permissions. While an agent is in control a gold frame lies over that screen and a Stop bar sits at the top; Stop, or Escape three times (Windows), turns screen control off at once. Nothing is typed while a Mimir permission dialog is open.

### Safer browser pairing

- **Mimir asks before a new browser links.** After you type the code into the Mimir extension, Mimir shows its own dialog and links the browser only when you say Yes, because any program on your computer could try codes. The extension's popup tells you to answer it. A browser you already paired connects as before.
- **Wrong codes slow down, then stop.** Each wrong code makes the next try wait longer, and after five, pairing stays closed until you press New code in Settings → Browser, which says so.
- **The browser link no longer falls over.** A malformed request from another program on your computer made the link restart, and a few in a row stopped it until you turned it off and on. Now such a request is just turned away.
